the cytokinin system is redundantly involved in the regulation of LR formation and growth.

cytokinin is involved in the control of LR formation on multiple levels by acting on the initiation and outgrowth of LR primordia and that cytokinin metabolism and signaling are redundantly required for this process.
the cytokinin signalling system is essential for lateral root formation and growth in plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of lateral roots by cytokinin and its role in the integration of environmental signals in the control of root system architecture.
the role of cytokinin metabolism and signaling in the regulation of lateral root development.
the regulation of lateral root formation in Arabidopsis and its interaction with the phytohormone cytokinin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cytokinin is a negative regulator of LR formation and growth, which is mediated by its biosynthesis and signalling genes.
the cytokinin system is a key regulator of LR initiation and growth.
cytokinin is involved in the regulation of LR formation and growth at different developmental stages and in different ways, but the molecular mechanisms of these actions are not well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cytokinin metabolism and cytokinin signalling genes redundantly control lateral root initiation, and that cytokinin and auxin interact in this process, but cytokinin and brassino- sterol act antagonistically.
the cytokinin signalling system is important for LR development, especially during early stages of LR formation.
cytokinin metabolism and signaling genes are important for the regulation of lateral root formation in Arabidopsis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytokinin system acts redundantly in LR initiation and elongation and that the different cytokinin signalling components are involved in different aspects of LR development.
the cytokinin system is important for LR formation and growth and that cytokinin signalling is essential for the integration of LR formation into the root system.

cytokinin is a key regulator of root development and that cytokinin metabolism and perception are essential components of a regulatory network that coordinates the formation of lateral roots with other developmental and environmental signals.
